title: Coefficient naturality of the concrete module/Ext resolution equivalence
statement: For any scheme X, nonnegative degree q, modules F and G and coefficient morphism phi:F -> G, the explicitly constructed moduleCohomologyExtResolutionEquiv from module-derived sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] to H [pqf-def-cohomology] commutes with their maps on phi. The equivalence is the composite of the standard module injective-resolution comparison, exact forgetting of homology, the inverse acyclic-resolution comparison on the forgotten resolution, the inverse concrete Ext/derived-sections comparison obtained from Hom complexes and the section adjunction, and Ext precomposition by the inverse free-abelian-terminal/constant-integers source isomorphism. All these maps are constructed; no arbitrary natural equivalence is chosen.

source.place: Tag 03FD, Lemma 21.12.4; Tag 01FT (derived sections); Tag 06XR (Ext by injective resolutions)

proof.text: Compute Ext by the standard abelian injective resolution and its Hom-complex cohomology classes. The from-single additive equivalence identifies the Hom complex with additive Hom applied degreewise. The sheafification/free-abelian/Yoneda adjunction identifies this Hom functor with sections. Derive this explicit natural isomorphism. Evaluation at the unique terminal generator identifies the terminal Ext source with the constant integer sheaf. These are concrete Lean constructions using Mathlib resolution, Hom-complex and adjunction isomorphisms.

Forgotten injective modules are acyclic for abelian sections. The explicit Ext/section comparison transports this vanishing to rightAcyclic, so the forgotten module resolution computes derived abelian sections. Compose its acyclic-resolution comparison with exact forgetting of the module section homology and the terminal Ext-source isomorphism to construct E.

Lift the coefficient morphism between standard module resolutions. Right-derived resolution naturality, exact-forgetting homology naturality, and acyclicComparison_naturality give the section-cohomology square. The explicit Hom-complex and section isomorphisms commute with postcomposition. Finally Ext associativity commutes postcomposition with terminal-source precomposition. Composing the squares gives the displayed coefficient naturality.
